stem.en: Kabir says "the antibiotic caused the bacteria to become resistant". What is the accurate order of events?

text.en: The resistant slip was already there in a few cells, by random copying error, before any drug. The drug removed the others. It selected; it did not cause. Give the same drug to a colony with no such slip and it cannot make one.

feedback.en: Test it: a colony with no resistant cells, dosed, dies completely and never becomes resistant. The slip must exist first.
A bacterium cannot change its ribosome's shape in its lifetime. Its child inherits its spelling. The population changed because of who was left.

text.en: The drug made the bacteria mutate faster.

feedback.en: Some drugs do raise slip rates, from VIII.1 L05, but the direction of the slip is still random. The drug still only removes; it never aims.

explanation.en: Mutation first, at random. Selection second, by the drug. Never the other way round.
